arc.mood: Level thirty-two, back in Menethil after a night in company. He'd made it as far from Loch Modan as the map allows, Gadgetzan, where nobody asks where a dwarf learned to build things, and then Charm Moonfeather asked him into a group and he went straight back north. Five hours with her: the Wetlands dig, three deaths in the tall grass, the Kraul, a gopher on a stick. On the road home he licked a stranger, sober. Still one drink. Still a bottle with a message in it, unopened.
arc.lookingFor: Someone who stays. Says it's a business partner for a brewery. It isn't.
runningBits: Two bottles unopened: the malt, and the message; the wine didn't count
Patted on the head, twice in two days
Everyone's keeping count, none with the right number
Kings make him check the exits
Nobody in Gadgetzan asks where a dwarf learned to build things
Keep your head down and your gopher busy

The rock won; the grass won three times
arc.frontRunner: Charm Moonfeather, now. Came and found him in Gadgetzan, ran him through the Wetlands and the Kraul for five hours, and moved up to friend. Volundr Embercast is still a friend on paper, a dwarf tank who said he'd find him tomorrow on the twelfth and hasn't. Nobody new has stuck; Lolyna Blackheart said hey first and meant it.
arc.wanted: WANTED: partner for a brewery that doesn't exist yet. Must tolerate noise, smoke, and questions about where you're from. Must laugh when I miss a wolf with a staff, but kindly. Dwarves need not apply, probably; the valley's full of them and not one asked. Inquire at Thunderbrew Distillery, loudest table.
arc.beat: Wednesday. He's parked in Menethil with a friend who keeps coming back, and he still hasn't bought her a drink. Next time Charm groups him, buy the round when it's done and say something to her out loud, even one line; that's the drink he finally raises back. The bottle stays corked. The schematic for Bright-Eye Goggles is worth building, sober, before the fourth pint gets near it. Ironband can keep waiting in Loch Modan. Setup: the record stops at Monday 11 PM. If he played Tuesday, it hasn't been published; check that the Dagnar dispatches task has "Require this computer" switched on.
arc.storySoFar:
Dagnar Barleigh was a Dark Iron demolitions engineer who walked away from a job in Loch Modan and never said why. He drifted to the Wildhammer in the Hinterlands, where an old shaman taught him to hold the fire in him instead of being held by it. He took a new name, learned to heal fast and ugly, and kept his engineering, which exploded past the fourth pint. He called the missing eyebrows quality control and said he wanted a partner for a brewery. It was not a brewery.

On the fourth of November 2026 he stepped into Coldridge Valley and found it wall to wall with dwarves and gnomes. A human named Malachi Zerbe pulled him into The Brave of Lordaeron. His first drink was a bottle of Dalaran Noir, which he insisted did not count. He missed a wolf three times with a staff he had forgotten he owned, reached Ironforge after eleven, and ended the night in Gol'Bolar Quarry with a quest about stolen blasting powder and a very still face. Then the record went dark for a week.

It came back on the eleventh with him past twenty and in company. Charm Moonfeather ran him through Redridge, Blackfathom Deeps and Ashenvale, where he led for once and died three times for it. At the Thandol Span he took a quest called The Dark Iron War and cut down his own people by the five, then walked a chained fire elemental out of Dun Modr. A party member cheered that there'd be no more dwarves, except Dagnar, who has to live with himself. He found a tank in Volundr Embercast, ran the Stockade with the guild, and earned his fourth totem. In the Wetlands the Wildhammer Clan started counting what he does, a stranger raised a drink he couldn't return, and a spirit at an old dig warned him about digging too deep into his past. He is thirty-one, still on one drink, and closer to Loch Modan than he has been in years.

The weekend went quiet. He sat in the Menethil tavern while an old sailor told the room about a sea giant, went back to Ironforge, and took three jobs from the Explorers' League, one of them from a prospector in Loch Modan, which he filed at the bottom. He walked into the Hall of Thanes twice and out twice, stood by the forge so long the city sent him home, and then spent a day with a fishing rod, a brazier and a workbench, levelling everything he could reach and blowing up nothing. A dwarf yelled that here we use our fires. Two strangers patted him on the head, two more gave him cards, and the spirit at the dig gave its warning five more times. Then he ran north through Arathi, past standing stones and a troll village, into Hillsbrad. He hasn't said a word out loud since Friday.

Then he kept going. He fished the Hillsbrad shore past a hundred and pulled up a bottle with a message in it, which he didn't open. He flew the long way to Duskwood, where it's always night, and sat by the Darkshire fire while a stranger called Artemis Star listed the road to the sleeping bag: the Barrens, Stonetalon, Loch Modan, Hillsbrad. Loch Modan, said like a stop on the way. He mined tin by night till a quarter to one. In Stormwind he followed Bazil Thredd's visitor up to the castle, found Lord Lescovar meeting a Defias man in his own garden, helped four strangers end it, and carried the report to the king, who gave him the Seal of Wrynn. Kings make him check the exits. He took the boat to Theramore, ran south through the Barrens and across the Shimmering Flats, and walked into Gadgetzan, a goblin town full of engineers where nobody asks where a dwarf learned to build things. He could get used to that, which is the trouble.

He didn't stay. Charm Moonfeather asked him into a group while he was still standing in Gadgetzan, the first time since the eleventh, and he went straight back north. At the Wetlands dig three more joined them to hunt raptors for their hides; somewhere in finding out what happened to Ardin Grassman he turned thirty-two, and he died three times in the tall grass doing it. Then Charm put a second group together and took them into Razorfen Kraul, quilboar and thorns and a death speaker, where you dig up tubers with a gopher on a stick and two of the group had words over whose tuber was whose. He kept his head down and his gopher busy. On the road home through Dustwallow he licked a stranger called Ragnar Deepstorm, sober, with not a pint to blame, and ended the night in Menethil. Charm is a friend now. He still hasn't bought her a drink.

Emmitt Brown.lastSaid: Congratulated a gnome on being named Pongo.
Emmitt Brown.note: Gnome. Thinks everyone is tall. Danced at the doors. I like him already.

Frizzle Cinderspark.lastSaid: Suggested everyone was short, not tall.
Frizzle Cinderspark.note: Gnome. Called the valley a family reunion. Asked after a Christmas card.

Fodrin Firebrand.note: Dwarf. Danced before he'd finished cheering.

Bargash Greybeard.lastSaid: Admired the pile of corpses, loudly, for the king.
Bargash Greybeard.note: Dwarf. Shouts for the forge and king. Likes a corpse pile.

Brother Borelgore.note: Dwarf. Looking for Phil. I hope he finds Phil.

Igneous Stonegarden.note: Dwarf. Says hello to everyone. Congratulates strangers.

Griym Firebeard.lastSaid: Called the wolf business the food chain.
Griym Firebeard.note: Dwarf. Has a theory about the food chain.

Doldrenn Stoneforge.note: Dwarf. Will join anyone for wolves. My kind of recruit.

Pus Pus.lastSaid: The shop was down, with feeling.
Pus Pus.note: Gnome. Tells jokes to other gnomes. Reports outages.

Anthéor Stonehymn.lastSaid: Declined to log out for the quest reward.
Anthéor Stonehymn.note: Dwarf. Knows what being a dwarf is about. Waited on a fire that owed him.

Embertempest Anvilmar.lastSaid: The campfire quest wouldn't pay out.
Embertempest Anvilmar.note: Dwarf. Smiled at a campfire that owed them a reward.

Náin Snowholdt.lastSaid: Suggested logging out and back in, out of character.
Náin Snowholdt.note: Dwarf. Wanted wolves early. Gives practical advice to strangers.

Charm Moonfeather.lastSaid: Whispered that her map was wrong and mine was right.
Charm Moonfeather.note: Ran the whole day: Redridge, Blackfathom, Ashenvale as a pair, the Thandol Span. Knows every cave. Shared quests and turned one of mine down. Came and found me in Gadgetzan on the sixteenth. Five hours: the Wetlands dig, then the Kraul.

Gawain Tenebris.lastSaid: Thanked everyone after the corporal got home.
Gawain Tenebris.note: Led the Redridge party. Kind to the mushroom gang. Called us gentlemen and scholars.

Rosa Luxemborne.lastSaid: Admitted to not trusting the mushroom gang.
Rosa Luxemborne.note: Asked to tag along in Redridge and did.

York Okismalle.note: Joined for the escort in Redridge.

Bazalnar Papadakis.note: Waited outside the Redridge cave. Ate the mushrooms.

Loria Liongard.lastSaid: Explained how to jump onto an invisible ledge.
Loria Liongard.note: Knew Blackfathom by heart. Set up camp for the buffs.

Tymir Beldorsson.lastSaid: Said yes to my need roll.
Tymir Beldorsson.note: Tenth run of Blackfathom for one eyeball.

Havo Shin.lastSaid: Asked where the sea boss lives.

Tecu Faeron.lastSaid: Joked there would be no more dwarves, except me.
Tecu Faeron.note: Thandol Span. Hates Dark Irons, cheerfully. Said I have to live with myself. True.

All Anon.note: Joined the party for a minute on the bridge.

Xyrei Daystar.note: Talked near me after the bridge.

Maxwell Hughes.note: Talked near me after the bridge.

Chudette Biwisi.lastSaid: Wanted a rogue for a lockbox.

Volundr Embercast.lastSaid: Warned the party about the beam. Then said rip.
Volundr Embercast.note: Dwarf, tank. I invited him; we've run things before, off the record. Says I level like a madman. Cheered at me in the Stockade. Gets lost.

Niko Ikory.lastSaid: Asked whether stealing a mage's mana in a mage city should be a crime.
Niko Ikory.note: Hunter, guild. Brought the quests and the sleeping bag. Pulled a boss early to beat my damage, and said so. Pats me on the head when passing.

Kristian Sparklewits.note: Gnome. Healed the Stockade so I could hit things. Gave Femto back as good as Femto gave.

Femto Eclipse.note: Human. Claims exile from the Scarlet Crusade. Insults gnomes in character, and is good at it.

Eldrin Belmont.lastSaid: Wished the Light on all of us.
Eldrin Belmont.note: Guild. Came for Dun Modr, left at the bridge.

Siligrun Stourheart.note: Guild. Waved at me in Ironforge.

Finwick Thaumwaver.note: Left us his explosives in Dun Modr.

Dergan Steelclad.note: Wanted into the group at Dun Modr.

Priscilla Meticcia.lastSaid: Realised I was the wrong shaman.
Priscilla Meticcia.note: Guild. Whispered me thinking we had run the Hall of Thanes together. We hadn't.

Galanar Bose.note: Raised a drink to me in the Wetlands. No idea why.

Alithia Evengale.note: Invited me out to the cursed wreck.

Thunidor Thunderkeg.note: Talked near me in the Wetlands.

Khaotikus Silvermoon.note: Talked near me in the Wetlands.

Minerva Moss.lastSaid: Asked if they made fishing trickier.
Minerva Moss.note: Dwarf. Fished the same canal. Lost a lot of fish, loudly.

Tolmin Ironwhisper.lastSaid: Told everyone to wash their backs.
Tolmin Ironwhisper.note: Dwarf. Yells about braziers. This isn't Stormwind; we use our fires here.

Dwalin Toadenheim.note: Patted me on the head in passing. Second one this week.

Brak Durnad.lastSaid: Gave me a card: a Menethil boarding axe.
Brak Durnad.note: Gifted a card in Menethil Harbor. I thanked him.

Brahnmar.lastSaid: Gave me a card: a Menethil marine's helm.
Brahnmar.note: Gifted a card in Menethil Harbor a few seconds after Brak. I thanked him.

Lim Jayhee.lastSaid: Announced to the inn at Southshore that they were back.
Lim Jayhee.note: Human. Loud about a marshal. Heard more than met.

Artemis Star.note: Skyborne. Knows the long road to the sleeping bag and gave it away for free. Said Loch Modan like it was just a stop.

Garrick Prowess.lastSaid: Asked if the sleeping bag was worth it.
Garrick Prowess.note: Human. Thought the route was the far side of the world. Asked the right question.

Jane Snowe.lastSaid: Offered free bracer enchants to anyone who would trade.
Jane Snowe.note: Human enchanter. Giving it away in the square at one in the morning.

Sapp Achino.lastSaid: Gave last call on lockpicking before logging off.
Sapp Achino.note: Skyborne. Opens locks for a living. Went to find one.

Eol Anglachel.lastSaid: Had me invited into the group for Lescovar.
Eol Anglachel.note: Night elf. Saw me waiting by the hedges and asked for me to be let in.

Theoden Lightstone.note: Dwarf. Fought in the lord's garden. Said thanks and left.

Akarui Hoshi.lastSaid: Asked to be let in, then said thanks.
Akarui Hoshi.note: Human. Late to the group, glad to be in it.

Tonkrin Brassbolt.lastSaid: Led the group for the Lescovar fight, then left.
Tonkrin Brassbolt.note: Led for a minute. Handed it to me on the way out.

Wymer Silverwood.lastSaid: Thanked everyone and left once the hides were in.
Wymer Silverwood.note: Human. Needed one more hide, same as everyone. Ran through the grass for it.

Surathis Bladefire.lastSaid: Said thanks as the dig group broke up.
Surathis Bladefire.note: Night elf. Ran the pulls at the dig. Warned us off the tall grass. Was right.

Marie Annette.lastSaid: Cheered when the last hide dropped.
Marie Annette.note: Human. Warlock, wishes soul shards came from a shop. Said you're welcome when I thanked an innkeeper.

Lolyna Blackheart.lastSaid: Left to run the Kraul again for a drop she needs.
Lolyna Blackheart.note: Human. Said hey first and meant it. Found the boss on her map. Got her upgrade.

Outrunner Nayus.note: Night elf. Hadn't been in the Kraul in years. Won the death speaker's scepter and gave it to me.

Allys Trueshot.lastSaid: Laughed at the useless gophers by the end.
Allys Trueshot.note: Night elf. Lost two tubers in the Kraul and said so, loudly. Laughed by the end.

Anara Wildwater.note: Night elf. Asked about the Kraul half an hour after we'd left it.

Ragnar Deepstorm.note: Got licked on the road through Dustwallow. By me. Sober.

Abock Glorymace.lastSaid: Warned us to stay away from the boss beam.
Abock Glorymace.note: Joined Charm's party in Hillsbrad. Figured out a Dalaran book, asked for a decurse and said thank you for it.

posts.title: Launch day
posts.text: Doors opened early. Coldridge Valley is wall-to-wall dwarves and gnomes, all shouting. Nothing's exploded yet. Give it a week.
posts.detail: Couldn't swing a dead cat without hitting a dwarf. Somebody else said that first.

posts.title: Coldridge, wall to wall
posts.text: Coldridge Valley, wall to wall, every dwarf and gnome on the realm shouting at once. I stood in it and asked nobody anything.
posts.detail: A gnome called Emmitt found everyone tall. Another, Frizzle, called it a family reunion. A dwarf named Doldrenn went off wolf-killing with a Náin. Nobody asked where I'm from. Nobody will, in a valley this full of dwarves.
posts.alt: Coldridge Valley on launch night, seen through three setup windows that would not close.

posts.title: Two to six
posts.text: Level six before the first pint. Wolves, troggs, a troll cave, two mail runs. Picked up skinning and mining because the mountain was offering.
posts.detail: The mornbrew went cold on the first delivery and had to go again. The earth sapta wouldn't turn in, twice. I was already carrying one. An engineer's mistake, not a shaman's.
posts.alt: Level six, in the snow, with a wolf and two troggs waiting their turn.

posts.title: The campfire
posts.text: Sat by Eric Brighthammer's fire with three dwarves. Anthéor Stonehymn said this was the whole point of being a dwarf. He's not wrong.
posts.detail: The fire paid me and wouldn't pay them. Embertempest Anvilmar and Anthéor were still waiting when I stood up. Náin Snowholdt suggested leaving and coming back. Anthéor declined.

posts.title: A guild, apparently
posts.text: Set my hearth at Thunderbrew Distillery, which tells you my priorities. Six minutes on, a human called Malachi Zerbe asked me into The Brave of Lordaeron. Said yes.
posts.detail: Hadn't said a word all night and still got invited. Either a good sign about them or a bad one about the night. The hall was loud within the minute. Humans, mostly, from the sound of it.

posts.title: Died once, so far
posts.text: Cheered for a lost gnome at fourteen past. Dead by fifteen past. Unrelated, as far as the gnome knows.
posts.detail: Ten percent off the gear. Walked back, finished Flintfire's shipment, then learned to cook boar ribs in beer, which is the first sensible thing anyone's taught me here.

posts.title: Camp cooking
posts.text: Charred the wolf, roasted the boar, got cooking up to five without burning anything that mattered. Then learned to roll a linen bandage. For other people, mostly.
posts.detail: No pint yet. The malt stays shut. The pilots at Steelgrill's wanted wendigo manes next, so that's where the evening went.

posts.title: The Grizzled Den
posts.text: Two dozen wendigo in one cave and I skinned most of them. One of their shamans objected at eight minutes to nine. Ten percent off the gear, again.
posts.detail: Died holding a carpenter's mallet I'd picked up six seconds earlier. Walked back. The cave was quiet by nine and skinning sat at seventy.

posts.title: Brewnall Village
posts.text: Walked into Brewnall Village on the lake and a Barleybrew handed me a barrel of Scalder to carry to his rival. No relation. A brewery, though. A real one.
posts.detail: Chill Breeze Valley first, then the lake, then Gnomeregan's front door for scale. Kharanos taught me a stoneclaw and a lightning shield on the way. Still nothing to drink. The Scalder is not mine to open.

posts.title: Gnomeregan's doorstep
posts.text: Leper gnomes at the front door of Gnomeregan, eighteen of them, every one promising to cut me. Took their cogs and gears instead. Razzle wants them for a machine.
posts.detail: Then up to Frostmane Hold, which is trolls, and a few leopards and bears on the way that nobody asked for. Rolled five bandages at two minutes to ten. Used none, which is the trick.

posts.title: The Recombobulator
posts.text: Died a third time at six past ten, to a troll at Frostmane Hold, which is what trolls are for. Three minutes later Razzle Sprysprocket fired up the Recombobulator with my gears.
posts.detail: It was meant to save the entire gnomish race. It needed more grease. Got driving gloves for the trouble and a short staff from Bellowfiz for walking back. Someone in Kharanos wants me to meet a visitor. Tomorrow. The malt's still shut.

posts.title: The forgotten staff
posts.text: Swung a staff at a winter wolf and missed three times running. I'd forgotten I owned it. Someone called Lime Rickey saw the whole thing and laughed, kindly.
posts.detail: First words I've put to anyone here, and they were an excuse. Lime said stay safe, friend. Whispered, not said out loud, so the letter stands.

posts.title: First night
posts.text: First night and I didn't say a word out loud. Twelve people talked near me and I listened, which you'd call progress and I'd call the cold.
posts.detail: Nobody asked where I'm from. Nobody will, in a valley this full of dwarves. Set my hearth at a distillery, joined a guild of humans with a brave name, died three times in the snow and minded the walks more. The malt they gave me for a delivery is still in the pack. Haven't decided who to open it with.

posts.title: Dalaran Noir
posts.text: First drink on the record. Carried a barrel of Shimmer Stout up Shimmer Ridge past the Frostmane, and the reward was a bottle of Dalaran Noir. Wine. From a bottle.
posts.detail: Tipsy for forty-six seconds, sober by quarter to. The Thunderbrews know what I am and handed me grapes anyway. The malt stays shut; this didn't count.

posts.title: Finding Warmth
posts.text: Watched Jarven Thunderbrew's barrels twice while he drank inside. Then north to the Tundrid Hills for quests called Finding Warmth, Treacherous Cold and Rime's Wrath.
posts.detail: A shaman sent to find warmth. I've been on that errand a while. Came away with a small bird that whistles, two linen bags and a binding called Avala's. Rime's Wrath twice, because once wasn't enough for someone.

posts.title: Ironforge
posts.text: Through the Gates of Ironforge at twenty past eleven. The great forge, a woman selling bread baked that morning, and a trade channel complaining the city was empty.
posts.detail: Learned to build a camp chair, the first thing I've been taught here that I'd actually sit in. The spirits also left word: a Call of Fire. We're acquainted. I'll go when I'm sober enough to be polite about it.

posts.title: Rats in the Tram
posts.text: Under the city a dwarf called Monty handed me a flute and a box and said the rats would walk in one by one. They did. Nine hundred points of experience for piping vermin.
posts.detail: Also took a carton of mystery meat for a man's brother Nipsy and asked no questions, because I've carried worse for less. The Deeprun Tram hums like a still about to go.

posts.title: Gol'Bolar Quarry
posts.text: Amberstill Ranch, where a girl was chasing a ram named Fluffy, then Gol'Bolar Quarry till past midnight. Rockjaw troggs. One word each. Mostly Destroy.
posts.detail: Someone there has lost blasting powder and wants it found. I said nothing. I'm the only dwarf in the quarry who knows what it's for, and it would be rude to look pleased. Mining up to seven. Bed at eleven past.

posts.title: The mushroom gang
posts.text: Back on the record in Redridge, in a party clearing Blackrock orcs out of a cave. Somebody waiting at the mouth of it had eaten several handfuls of the wrong mushrooms.
posts.detail: A week went by off the books and I came back a good deal further along than level six; don't ask me where it went. Gawain Tenebris ran the party and Charm Moonfeather knew the cave. I said one thing out loud all afternoon: I'd rather be drinkin'. Then we walked a wounded corporal called Keeshan home, slowly.

posts.title: Blackfathom Deeps
posts.text: Charm Moonfeather pulled five of us together for Blackfathom Deeps. I went in as the healer and asked, politely, to roll need on healer gear. They said yes.
posts.detail: A drowned temple full of naga and cultists who want the Old Gods back. Loria Liongard knew where every chest was hiding; Tymir Beldorsson was on his tenth run for one murloc's eyeball. Came out with a manuscript, a bag of brain stems and new boots. Learned Stormstrike somewhere in the wet.

posts.title: Three in twenty minutes
posts.text: Charm and I took Ashenvale as a pair, me leading for once. Died at two minutes to eight, again at quarter past, and again three minutes after that.
posts.detail: Satyrs at Satyrnaar, then whatever lived between there and Splintertree Post, which turned out to be an orc town. Raene's Cleansing took four turn-ins and a rod that needed fixing twice. Set my hearth at Astranaar after. The trees there don't explode.

posts.title: The Dark Iron War
posts.text: Thandol Span, and a quest called The Dark Iron War. Fifteen Dark Iron dwarves, five saboteurs, five tunnelers, five demolitionists. I didn't count out loud.
posts.detail: Tecu Faeron and Astronova Starwhisper made us four. The Dark Irons had wired the bridge, and I know how they tie a charge; I said nothing about that either. We destroyed the cache and the bridge is still standing. They paid me in Ez-Thro Dynamite, five sticks, which is only funny if you're me.

posts.title: Spark of Freedom
posts.text: The Dark Irons at Dun Modr kept a fire elemental in chains. We walked it out. It said the same word over and over, and the word was fire.
posts.detail: Tecu went looking for a captive dwarf to rescue and found this instead. It didn't thank anybody. Fire doesn't. I walked next to it the whole way and kept my hands to myself.

posts.title: Except for Dagnar
posts.text: Tecu Faeron left the party cheering that there'd be no more dwarves. Except Dagnar, who has to live with himself.
posts.detail: I said I was sorry for what they'd done to everyone. I meant the Dark Irons. Tecu meant it as a joke, and it was one, and I laughed. Then I stood on the bridge a while.

posts.title: Water Walking
posts.text: Trained up after the bridge. Water Walking, Flametongue Totem, and a totem that keeps fire off people.
posts.detail: Loria asked in the Deeps whether anyone could walk on water. Four hours late, I can. The fire one I'll keep in the pack and not think about why.

posts.title: Volundr
posts.text: Asked Volundr Embercast into a group. A dwarf and a tank, and his first words were that I was levelling like a madman.
posts.detail: I didn't argue. Niko Ikory turned up with three quests for the Stockade and a plan to go through the Wetlands first. I said I hate Stormwind. Niko said the dwarf city's better. Nobody disagreed.

posts.title: Dun Modr, again
posts.text: Back to Dun Modr with a guild crew who still needed it. I'd done it the night before, so I came to help and told them the fire elemental was an escort.
posts.detail: Walked it out a second time. It still said fire. Niko said that's what you get for helping elementals, and claimed to know. Eldrin Belmont and Kristian Sparklewits made five; Eldrin left at the bridge, blessing everyone in the Light, which was kind of him.

posts.title: Someone in the bag
posts.text: Niko Ikory laid out a sleeping bag before the Stockade, for the experience. I said Niko just wanted someone in the bag.
posts.detail: Niko said dwarven men are very attractive. Volundr said thank you before I could. Three of us in a little bag, five by the end, and that's all anyone's getting about it.

posts.title: The Stockade
posts.text: Six quests in one prison. Targorr, Deepfury, Bazil Thredd, Dextren Ward. Kristian healed, so I hit things.
posts.detail: Femto Eclipse spent the walk in insulting the gnome, in character, and was good at it. They love their harnesses in there; I said so. Deepfury's head was for a man in the Wetlands, which is the kind of errand I understand.

posts.title: I didn't do it
posts.text: Died in the Stockade at three minutes to seven when the next boss came early. I said I didn't do it. I didn't.
posts.detail: Niko owned up: wanted to beat my damage and needed more targets. Femto blamed the gnome on principle. On the way out I flexed at Volundr, for no reason, and he took it well.

posts.title: Four totems
posts.text: Trained Windfury and took the Call of Air out to the Circle of East Binding. Came back with an air totem. That makes four.
posts.detail: Also learned Reincarnation, which means the spirits will stand me back up now and then, and two engineering plans: a target dummy and a silver contact. Nothing's exploded. Volundr went home early and said he'd find me tomorrow.

posts.title: Wrong shaman
posts.text: A guildmate, Priscilla Meticcia, whispered that we'd just run the Hall of Thanes together. We hadn't. Another shaman, a name a bit like mine.
posts.detail: I said it was all good, and it was. Nice to be mistaken for someone who goes places. Rode the boat to Theramore first thing that morning and came straight back.

posts.title: The Wildhammer are counting
posts.text: Turned in Deepfury's head at Ironbeard's Tomb, and the Wildhammer Clan started keeping a ledger on me. Neutral.
posts.detail: They taught me to hold the fire. Neutral sounds about right. Took two of their jobs on the spot, one called Trying Times.

posts.title: Thelgen Rock
posts.text: Stopped to mine at Thelgen Rock. Died twice, three minutes apart. The rock won.
posts.detail: Mining went up to seventy-five on the way, so call it a trade. Nobody saw. That's the main thing.

posts.title: Galanar Bose
posts.text: A stranger called Galanar Bose raised a drink to me. I didn't have one to raise back.
posts.detail: No idea what it was for. I'll take it. The malt's still shut, which is starting to look like a decision.

posts.title: Aman
posts.text: At the dig by Ironbeard's Tomb an archaeologist summoned a spirit called Aman. It warned that digging too deep into your past might bring an abrupt end to your future.
posts.detail: The archaeologist called it a mystery of the past and a key to the future. He called it up four times while I was there. I didn't ask it anything.

posts.title: The Cursed Crew
posts.text: Alithia Evengale and Jaxtis Unseen took me out to a wreck full of drowned sailors who still wanted brains. Thirteen sailors, five marines.
posts.detail: Alithia said thank you and left. I died on the same ship at nineteen past, on my own, which is how ships go. Learned Improved Stormstrike that afternoon.

posts.title: Trying Times
posts.text: Pulled down Dragonmaw war banners, thinned the razormaws and cleared the crocs for the Wildhammer. Trying Times, the quest was called. Fair.
posts.detail: Saltspray Glen smells like a still with the lid off. The orcs said a lot in Orcish and none of it was hello. Spent the whole day in one swamp and didn't mind.

posts.title: Hargin's leg
posts.text: Started the day in the tavern at Menethil Harbor. An old sailor called Hargin Mundar told the room about a sea giant he saw once, and hiccuped between sentences.
posts.detail: He'd clear the gnolls out himself, he said, but the leg. Then he was sick on the floor. I didn't order anything. Still one drink on the record, with a tavern right there.

posts.title: A pat on the head
posts.text: Back in Ironforge. Niko Ikory walked past and patted me on the head, like a dog that had done well.
posts.detail: Didn't stop, didn't say why. I'll take it. In a guild this loud, a pat on the head counts as a conversation.

posts.title: Ironband wants me
posts.text: The Explorers' League handed me three jobs at once: titan mythology, some Reclaimers out in Desolace, and a prospector called Ironband who wants me.
posts.detail: Ironband's in Loch Modan. I put that one at the bottom of the log. The other two are a long way from anywhere I've been, which is the appeal.

posts.title: The Hall of Thanes
posts.text: Walked into the Hall of Thanes twice and walked out twice. Bronzebeard kings sit there.
posts.detail: Nobody stopped me. Nobody in this city has looked twice at me yet, which is either the beard or the name. Barleigh's doing its job.
posts.alt: Dagnar on the red-and-gold carpet leading into the Hall of Thanes in Ironforge, carved stone pillars on either side.

posts.title: Sent home for being quiet
posts.text: Came back to Ironforge after dark and stood by the forge for forty minutes without a word. The city sent me home for being too quiet.
posts.detail: Behind me, two night elves cheered and bowed at each other like old friends. Nobody did that at me. I didn't try. Next time, a drink I can raise back.

posts.title: A rod and a canal
posts.text: Sat at the water in Ironforge with a rod I'd never held. An hour and a hundred-odd fish later, I was a journeyman.
posts.detail: Mud snapper, mostly. Some catfish, some smallfish, one mana potion that somebody else lost. A dwarf called Minerva Moss kept yelling that my fish got away. Quiet work. The fire didn't mind it.

posts.title: We use our fires here
posts.text: Tolmin Ironwhisper yelled across the room that I could use the braziers. This wasn't Stormwind. Here we use our fires.
posts.detail: Then he yelled at everyone to wash their backs. I liked him immediately. A dwarf who shouts about fire is a dwarf I can understand.

posts.title: Cooked the catch
posts.text: Thirty-six wolf steaks, six spiced, then thirty-nine of the snapper I'd pulled out of the canal. Cooking went from ten to ninety in fifteen minutes.
posts.detail: Just before I lit the brazier, a dwarf called Dwalin Toadenheim walked by and patted me on the head. That's twice in two days. I'm starting to think I look like I've done well. Picked up a recipe for beer-basted ribs. Noted.

posts.title: Ninety-eight, no bangs
posts.text: Rolled thirty-four bandages, then smelted copper and made bolts and eight modulators. First aid past a hundred, engineering at ninety-eight.
posts.detail: Sober the whole time, so nothing went off. Eyebrows intact. It's not as satisfying as you'd think.

posts.title: Two cards in Menethil
posts.text: Walked into Menethil Harbor and two strangers handed me cards inside a minute. Brak Durnad gave me a boarding axe. Brahnmar gave me a marine's helm.
posts.detail: Paper ones, for the card game everyone's playing. I thanked them both. Nobody's given me anything for free since the shaman, and hers cost everything.

posts.title: The warning again
posts.text: Spent the afternoon in Menethil. Out at the dig the archaeologist kept calling up the spirit, and five times it said the same thing about digging too deep into your past.
posts.detail: The innkeeper kept saying the commotion had died down. Somebody got rough with a smuggler and he talked. I sat it out. Some warnings you only need once. I've had six.

posts.title: Over the hills
posts.text: Went north through Arathi at a run. A circle of standing stones, an orc farm, a troll village. Then over the border into Hillsbrad, which I'd never seen.
posts.detail: Dug two lumps of silver on the way. The League of Arathor have started a ledger on me too. Neutral. Everyone's keeping count of me lately, and none of them have the right number.

posts.title: A bottle in the catch
posts.text: Fished the shore below Hillsbrad for twenty minutes. Rainbow fin, a few blackmouth, and a bottle with a message in it.
posts.detail: Fishing went past a hundred. I haven't opened the bottle. Somebody wrote to whoever found it, and I'm not sure that's me.

posts.title: Crime and Punishment
posts.text: Flew the long way round to Duskwood, where it's always night. Took a job called Crime and Punishment into Darkshire and came out with a town clerk's mittens.
posts.detail: The flight crossed Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes. I watched the road, not the mountain. In Darkshire a man said he can't visit his father's grave in peace anymore. Nobody can, here.

posts.title: The long way round
posts.text: By the fire in Darkshire, Artemis Star talked Garrick Prowess through the road to a sleeping bag. Barrens, Stonetalon, Loch Modan, Hillsbrad.
posts.detail: Garrick said that was the far side of the world. Artemis said it was a haul but worth it, and wished us safe adventures. Loch Modan, said like a stop on the way. For most people it is.

posts.title: Tin by night
posts.text: Mined Duskwood in the dark till a quarter to one. Tin and silver, mostly. Mining went from seventy-seven to ninety-five.
posts.detail: The town crier shouted twice that an abomination was coming up the road. Somebody dealt with it. All's well in Darkshire, he said. I smelted one copper bar back in Ironforge and called it a night.

posts.title: The lord's garden
posts.text: Bazil Thredd had a visitor in the Stockade. I followed the description up to the castle, to a lord called Lescovar meeting a Defias man in his own garden.
posts.detail: Four strangers and I waited by the hedges for them to finish talking. Eol Anglachel had me pulled into the group. It was quick. Theoden Lightstone said thanks, and the group was gone inside a minute.
posts.alt: Dagnar's totems glowing in the garden of Stormwind Keep during the fight with Lord Lescovar.

posts.title: Seal of Wrynn
posts.text: Carried the report on the Defias Brotherhood to the king. They gave me the Seal of Wrynn for it.
posts.detail: Kings make me want to check the exits. I checked them. Then I left with the seal.

posts.title: Gadgetzan
posts.text: Took the boat to Theramore and dropped off two errands. Then south through the Barrens, down the Great Lift, across the Shimmering Flats. Gadgetzan.
posts.detail: A goblin town full of engineers, in a desert, with a bruiser on every corner. Nobody here asks where a dwarf learned to build things. I could get used to that.

posts.title: Back to the Wetlands
posts.text: Charm Moonfeather asked me into a group while I was still in Gadgetzan. First time since the eleventh. I went back north.
posts.detail: Mosshide gnolls, nine lumps of flint for a quest called Fire Taboo, a dozen fen creepers. She kept the count in the party line. I carried the flint, which is the closest I get to fire taboo.
posts.alt: Dagnar and Charm Moonfeather in the grey swamp grass of the Wetlands, a gnoll fight just finished.

posts.title: Three at the dig
posts.text: Three more came to the dig in the Wetlands: Wymer Silverwood, Surathis Bladefire and Marie Annette. We hunted raptors for their hides.
posts.detail: Surathis warned us off the tall grass early. The raptors lived in the tall grass. Marie said you're welcome when I thanked an innkeeper, which I'm counting as the first conversation.

posts.title: Thirty-two
posts.text: Found out what happened to Ardin Grassman, and somewhere in the finding out I turned thirty-two.
posts.detail: The staff I forgot I owned on launch night, I swung all evening, and by the end I mostly hit things with it. Won a schematic for goggles on a need roll too. Nobody else in the group builds anything.
posts.alt: Night at the Wetlands excavation: Dagnar turning in a quest by the scaffolding, Surathis Bladefire beside him and Marie Annette below.

posts.title: The tall grass
posts.text: Died three times at the dig: twenty past seven, twelve to eight, a minute to eight. All three in the grass.
posts.detail: Lost the hunter in it once and said so. The last time I said ugh first, which is as close to a speech as I got. The final hide dropped four minutes later and I said thanks.
posts.alt: Dagnar's spirit view in tall swamp grass at the Wetlands dig, the party fighting a raptor in the clearing ahead.

posts.title: Razorfen Kraul
posts.text: Charm put together a second group and took us into Razorfen Kraul. Quilboar, thorns, and a death speaker.
posts.detail: Lolyna Blackheart, Outrunner Nayus and Allys Trueshot. Won a heart of Agamaggan on a need roll and a feathered headdress. Walked Willix the Importer out alive. Goblins pay their debts in rings.

posts.title: The gopher
posts.text: In the Kraul you dig up tubers with a gopher on a stick. Two of the group had words over whose tuber was whose. I kept my head down and my gopher busy.
posts.detail: It kept wiggling its whiskers at me. Best company in the place. On the way out Nayus handed me the death speaker's scepter he'd won, said it went with a shield. Charm thanked us for being chill.

posts.title: Sober
posts.text: Licked a stranger called Ragnar Deepstorm on the road home through Dustwallow. Sober. Not a pint to blame.
posts.detail: Before that, turned in the Crone of the Kraul and got a quilboar blaster for it, which is a gun, which I'll be taking apart. Ended the night in Menethil. Hargin Mundar was still telling the room about the sea giant.

posts.title: Volundr, again
posts.text: Charm put a party together in Hillsbrad and Volundr Embercast walked into it. Five days gone. Didn't say where. I didn't ask.
posts.detail: Niko came too, and a newcomer called Abock Glorymace who'd just worked out a Dalaran book and wanted to know where the drowned city was. Charm said Stranglethorn, probably. Nobody argued with her.

posts.title: The sleeping bag
posts.text: Charm whispered me the way, then admitted her map was wrong and mine was right. We ended up outside Dalaran in somebody's sleeping bag.
posts.detail: The one thing I said all afternoon, I said to the party: three percent experience if you sleep. Practical. Then the mace skill climbed forty points in the sewers and I stopped counting.

posts.title: The beam
posts.text: Under Dalaran there's a boss with a beam. Abock said stay out of it. Volundr said watch out for it. I died in it at half past five, and again at quarter to six.
posts.detail: Volundr said rip, which from a tank is a eulogy. Niko asked whether stealing a mage's mana in a mage city ought to be a crime. I'd have answered, but I was dead.

posts.title: Friend of the Kirin Tor
posts.text: Four hours in the ruins: green samples, starving arcana, a heart of disruption. The Kirin Tor called me a friend for it, and I came out thirty-three.
posts.detail: The party broke up at five past eight, everyone at once, the way good nights end. Still no round bought. Volundr's back, though, and he knows where the beam is now. So do I.

recipes.note: Charred is the recipe, not the result.
Five at the start of the day. Used most of them in the Deeps.
